questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: McGill University has a strong reputation within neuroscience and psychology, and the courses offered there lived up to my expectations. Additionally, I had heard a lot of good things from friends who had previously been on exchange in Montreal.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, although most of it was tied up in various emails, making it hard to keep track of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received plenty of information about online introduction seminars and events, since Montreal was heavily locked down when I arrived. Very helpfully, an academic advisor reached out to me to schedule a meeting, in which we discussed my course load, and where she made it very clear that I could contact her at all times if I needed any kind of assistance with my stay at McGill.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, there were plenty of Facebook groups with the purpose of finding student accommodation. Plateau and Mile End are really nice and vibrant areas with lots of young people and not too expensive housing (much cheaper than the accommodation provided by the university).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was done through the online portal Minerva. It could be a bit tricky to navigate some of the terms they used to describe my eligibility to apply for different courses. I had to contact several professors who offered courses that I wanted to take in order to be eligible to take them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Administrative services with normal phone hours

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to register for three out of the four courses that I initially wanted to take. The last course was not open for me to register for, even after getting confirmation from the professor teaching the course, due to some administrative errors by the department of psychology.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare a list of courses before the registration opens and contact any professors offering courses where you have to get prerequisites approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the content was quite high, but the assessments were generally quite easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lectures compared to classes than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOL 307 – Behavioural Ecology
PSYC 315 – Computational Psychology
PSYC 318 – Behavioural Neuroscience 2
PSYC 443 – Affective Neuroscience

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PSYC 318/443. These courses offered very interdisciplinary approaches to neuroscience, in a way that courses at UCPH do not. Contained the full range of philosophical, psychological, physiological, behavioural, and molecular/cellular aspects of the given areas.
